candidates.name: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
support_spans: progressive dyspnea, fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
Right upper-lobe opacities
Interval enlargement of parenchymal abnormality with ground-glass halo and progressive central cavitation
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging studies suggest a chronic pulmonary infection, and the presence of Aspergillus species in the bronchoalveolar lavage and surgical pathology supports this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Aspergilloma
support_spans: Admission CT: Right pneumothorax with interval progression of aspergilloma and suspected bronchopleural fistula
Bronchoalveolar lavage: Aspergillus niger isolated from right middle and lower lobe samples
candidates.why: The patient's imaging studies and laboratory tests confirm the presence of an aspergilloma, a type of fungal infection.

candidates.name: Invasive aspergillosis
support_spans: Aspergillus IgG: >200 mg/L
A. niger IgE: 1.04 kU/L (weakly positive)
candidates.why: The patient's laboratory tests suggest an invasive aspergillosis infection, which is consistent with the clinical presentation and imaging studies.

candidates.name: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
support_spans: mild intermittent asthma since childhood
A. niger IgE: 1.04 kU/L (weakly positive)
candidates.why: The patient's history of asthma and positive IgE test suggest an allergic reaction to Aspergillus, which may be contributing to the clinical presentation.

candidates.name: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
support_spans: Bronchoalveolar lavage: Aspergillus niger isolated from right middle and lower lobe samples
Surgical pathology: Acute exudative pleuritis with pleural/subpleural abscess formation and degenerated hyphae on Grocott methenamine silver stain
candidates.why: The patient's laboratory tests and surgical pathology confirm the diagnosis of chronic pulmonary aspergillosis.
